title: California joint insurance gradients are sensitive to income and wildfire-risk cut points
source_unit: Sensitivity screens of California ZIP-level FAIR/private-market decisions joined to ACS and CDI exposure context
geography: California ZIP/ZCTA approximations with county exposure context

denominator.unit: all-dimension joined ZIP rows; cells reported separately

low_income_high_risk_nonrenewal_rate.unit: percent among voluntary renewed plus nonrenewed decisions; 75 ZIP rows

low_income_low_risk_nonrenewal_rate.unit: percent among voluntary renewed plus nonrenewed decisions; 84 ZIP rows

high_income_high_risk_nonrenewal_rate.unit: percent among voluntary renewed plus nonrenewed decisions; 546 ZIP rows

high_income_low_risk_nonrenewal_rate.unit: percent among voluntary renewed plus nonrenewed decisions; 865 ZIP rows

observations.method: Recomputed decision-weighted nonrenewal cells under three predefined income/risk splits: $50,000/12.1%, joined-sample medians ($86,771/$10.1%), and lower-income/upper-risk quartile boundaries ($64,000/20.6%).
observations.uncertainty: Cut-point changes alter composition and cell sizes; the underlying joins retain ZIP/ZCTA approximation, county-level modeled exposure, 2015-versus-2022 timing mismatch, and denominator differences.
observations.subgroup: Four income-by-risk cells under each sensitivity definition.
observations.counterinterpretation: Because the low-income risk ordering reverses under the $50,000 definition, the original low-income/high-risk contrast cannot be treated as a stable wildfire-risk gradient.

related_sources.claim: Local output records all sensitivity cut points and cell rates.
related_sources.access_boundary: Sensitivity does not solve causal or denominator limitations.

boundary: This record qualifies the California joint insurance screen by showing sensitivity to grouping definitions. It does not establish causality, household affordability, coverage adequacy, repairs, moves, lending effects, or political response.
